_about: The Tavern's overheard lines (web lib/tavernGossip.ts, eight reworded to be true in the port).

say: I heard there's a forge out there that melts two bits of raid loot into one better one.
Melts. So you lose both?
You lose both.
Two of the same boss piece on the anvil and you get the better one back.
Two for one?
Two for one, and a bit of scrap for the smith.
Whole gunwharf up past the reef now. That's where they keep the ship.
Keep it? I thought you just sailed it.
Fishing boat won't go past the sea gate. Won't and can't. They tell you at the gate.
Man came in last week with a hull that does near double the speed of mine. Would not say what he paid.
Every raid item you own has to be mounted before you sail or it may as well be in a drawer.
Gold band on the dial. Not the green. The gold.
And if you miss it?
Then you caught a fish like everybody else.
Bait's not decoration. Right worm and they're on the hook before you've settled.
lines.from: over the top of a tankard

say: Sell to the buyer out in the zone and he takes his cut. Sail it home to the market and you get the lot.
Sailing home takes an hour.
Then that's what your hour is worth.
Water goes different colors the further out you get. That's not the light. That's how deep you are.
Patches of water where they're practically jumping in. Moves about. Never in the same place twice.
He measured it. Wrote the length down and everything.
Was it big?
It was the biggest one he'd caught. That's all a record is.
Hook does the holding, reel does the hauling, rod does the rest. People buy them in the wrong order.
Chain enough perfect casts together and something changes. I've never managed more than four.
Crew sat on a bench earn nothing. Crew sat in a bunk at the hall come out better than they went in.
Send them out on a trawl and they fish while you're not even here.
And they just hand it over when they're back?
They hand it over.
Lost two on the deep route last month.
Lost?
Lost. They don't come back from that one.
Fortune's the one that keeps them alive. Enough of it and the route stops being able to take anybody.
Everyone talks about power. Power decides how it went. Fortune decides what you brought home.
Skipper I know runs the same four hands every voyage and won't hear a word about swapping.
One voyage in a hundred comes back loaded. Properly loaded. I've seen it once.
lines.from: over the top of a tankard

say: Board up at the charterhouse posts where they're going. Read it before you sign anything.
Gauntlet does not care how good you think you are.
You go again after?
Everybody goes again after.
There are crews out there where the dead stay dead.
Why would anybody.
Ask them. They won't sail any other way.
Raid turns halfway through and the sea itself starts interfering. Nobody warns you the first time.
Board of bounties opens once you've put a chapter behind you. Finish it and they post another.
End of a chapter they make you choose what kind of ship she is. You don't get to change your mind.
Rocks out there you can actually land on. Half of them have something buried.
You need the bearing first. No bearing, no dig, doesn't matter how long you stand there with a shovel.
Bottles wash up with bits of writing in them. I've got four and they're clearly one story.
Chart room does a new set of puzzles every week. Solving them fills the map in.
Fills it in with what?
Places. And they pay for the ones you find.
Homestead's yours to build on. Mine's still mostly weeds.
Tally house posts the day's orders. Three of them, and a fresh three the moment you're done.
Have you talked to Finn before?
Once.
Full of himself, isn't he.
Finn'll give you work. He'll also make sure you know he's doing you a favor.
Meg's been on that scale thirty years. She knows exactly who you are and she won't say.
Matty tried to get me to put my whole hold on the Catfish Jackpot.
He called it a position. It's a bet. He knows it's a bet.
Old Marlow hasn't moved in years. Sits out in the deep and lets the sea come past him.
Quiet Fitch said three words to me and I've thought about all three since.
Grey Nance keeps the count of who goes down to the oldest water and comes back up.
And the ones who don't?
She keeps that count too.
Yoon's got a rod no shop will ever stock. Getting him to part with it is the hard bit.
Dennis told me a story about the expeditions that took the whole of last orders. I don't remember how it ended. I don't think it did.
Cass Turbot dives the wrecks and comes back with stories.
Are they true?
Some of them.
Rue Bream knows everything about everybody out there and remembers all of it. Be nice to Rue.
Turn up to the same person day after day and they start talking to you differently. Takes months.
They've each got a fish they love. Bring them that one and it's worth a week of turning up.
Doby and Kat walked me through my first cast. Still don't know which of them was in charge.
Den's through the town. Chips only, and there's a limit on what you can buy in a day.
Probably for the best.
Slots have one line that pays out like nothing else. Catfish all the way across.
Parlour deals the questions like cards. Answer enough of them right and they start calling you a king.
First one past the post takes it. Doesn't matter how close second was.
Fresh hands turn up at the Crew Hall every so often. Worth looking in.
Start over once you've topped out and everything pays double after.
Start over.
Start over. Some people have done it more than once.
Past the hundred it stops being levels and starts being something you spend.
He's got a rod he built himself, piece by piece. Took him the better part of a year.
Badges for near enough everything. I've got one for a thing I did by accident.
This is the third time this week they've watered it.
You keep drinking it.
I keep drinking it.
Weather's turning. You can smell it off the harbor.
He named the boat after his mother.
That's sweet.
It is not. You should hear what he calls it in a squall.
Biggest thing I ever hooked snapped the line and I've been thinking about it for two years.
Price of worms. That's all I'm going to say about it. The price of worms.
She came in soaked, put a fish on the bar, and left. Nobody's touched it.
I sailed four hours out and four hours back and caught two sardines.
Good day then.
There's a lad who moors at the same spot every morning and just sits there.
Never trust a captain whose boots are dry.
My hands haven't been warm since Tuesday.
He says he's seen the bottom.
Nobody's seen the bottom.
He says he's seen the bottom.
If it's got teeth and it's bigger than the boat, cut the line. That's the whole of it.
Whoever's been sleeping in the back room, we know. We all know.
I've been out there a year and the sea has still not run out of places I haven't been.
Same story every time he tells it, except the fish gets longer.
Do not let him buy the next round. Trust me on this.
The quiet ones out on the water are the ones worth stopping for.
Tide's wrong tonight. Don't ask me how I know.
Two of them came in arguing about a fish neither of them caught.
Every captain in here thinks they're one good haul from being comfortable.
He put his whole purse on the wheel.
And?
And he's behind you. Don't turn round.
I like it out there at night. Everything's further away.
You can hear the deep water before you're in it. Different sound off the hull.
Nobody's beaten her time on that run. Nobody's come close.
Bought the hat. Regret nothing.
